import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path


# Stop-hook decision helpers.  Keep the hook protocol payload unchanged:
# the Stop hook always receives a JSON event on stdin and must print a
# single JSON decision object on stdout.
def _allow():
    return {"decision": {"decision": "allow"}}


def _block(reason):
    return {"decision": {"decision": "block", "reason": reason}}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Transcript loading / message extraction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _load_records(transcript_path):
    """Read a Claude transcript file.

    Transcripts are normally JSONL, but accept a top-level JSON array as well.
    Return a list of record dicts, or [] when the file is missing/invalid.
    """
    if not transcript_path:
        return []

    try:
        path = Path(transcript_path)
        raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError):
        return []

    # Support whole-file JSON exports (a top-level array, or an object with a
    # "messages"/"transcript" array) in addition to JSONL.
    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
        if isinstance(data, list):
            return [item for item in data if isinstance(item, dict)]
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            for key in ("messages", "transcript"):
                items = data.get(key)
                if isinstance(items, list):
                    return [item for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        pass

    records = []
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            record = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if isinstance(record, dict):
            records.append(record)
    return records


def _extract_text(content):
    """Best-effort extraction of plain text from a transcript content value."""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content

    if isinstance(content, list):
        parts = []
        for block in content:
            if isinstance(block, str):
                parts.append(block)
            elif isinstance(block, dict):
                if block.get("type") == "text" and isinstance(block.get("text"), str):
                    parts.append(block["text"])
                elif isinstance(block.get("text"), str):
                    parts.append(block["text"])
        return "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)

    if isinstance(content, dict):
        return _extract_text(content.get("content", ""))

    return ""


def _is_tool_result_message(record):
    """True when a user-role record is only carrying tool results."""
    message = record.get("message") if isinstance(record, dict) else None
    content = message.get("content") if isinstance(message, dict) else record.get("content")
    if isinstance(content, list) and content:
        return all(
            isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_result"
            for block in content
        )
    return False


def _message_role(record):
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return None

    top_type = record.get("type")
    if top_type in ("user", "assistant"):
        return top_type

    message = record.get("message")
    if isinstance(message, dict):
        role = message.get("role")
        if role in ("user", "assistant"):
            return role

    role = record.get("role")
    if role in ("user", "assistant"):
        return role

    return None


def _message_content(record):
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return ""
    message = record.get("message")
    if isinstance(message, dict):
        content = message.get("content")
        if content is not None:
            return content
    return record.get("content", "")


def _collect_messages(records):
    """Return [(role, text), ...] for user/assistant messages.

    Tool-result user turns are skipped because they are not real user
    instructions.  Assistant turns are kept even when they have no text so the
    caller can tell whether the *last* assistant turn actually contains a
    final text answer.
    """
    messages = []
    for record in records:
        role = _message_role(record)
        if role not in ("user", "assistant"):
            continue
        if role == "user" and _is_tool_result_message(record):
            continue
        text = _extract_text(_message_content(record)).strip()
        messages.append((role, text))
    return messages


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Formatting detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SHORT_ANSWER_REQUEST_PATTERNS = [
    r"\b(?:short|bare|one-word|single-word|brief|concise|direct)\s+(?:answer|response|reply|format)\b",
    r"\b(?:answer|respond|reply)\s+(?:with|using|in)?\s*(?:only|just|nothing\s+but|no\s+more\s+than)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:short|bare|one-word|single-word|brief|concise|direct)?\s*(?:answer|response|reply|name|word|number|value)\b",
    r"\b(?:answer|respond|reply)\s+(?:only|just)\s+(?:with\s+)?(?:the\s+)?(?:short|bare|one-word|single-word|brief|concise|direct)?\s*(?:answer|response|reply|name|word|number|value)\b",
    r"\b(?:answer|respond|reply)\s+with\s+the\s+(?:name|word|number|short\s+answer|answer)\s+only\b",
    r"\b(?:only|just|nothing\s+but)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:short|bare|one-word|single-word|brief|concise|direct)?\s*(?:answer|name|word|number|value|response|reply)\b",
    r"\b(?:give|provide|return|state|say|tell\s+me)\s+(?:only|just)\s+the\b",
    r"\b(?:just|only)\s+(?:give|provide|return|state|say|tell\s+me)\s+the\b",
    r"\b(?:give|provide|return|state|say)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:name|word|number|short\s+answer|answer)\s+(?:only|just)\b",
    r"\b(?:only|just)\s+(?:one\s+)?(?:word|name|number)\b",
    r"\banswer\s+only\b",
    r"\banswer\s+in\s+one\s+word\b",
    r"\b(?:with|using)\s+(?:only|just)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:short|bare)?\s*(?:answer|name|word|number)\b",
    r"\bno\s+(?:explanation|commentary|extra|additional\s+text|justification)\b",
    r"\bwithout\s+(?:any\s+)?(?:explanation|commentary|markdown|formatting|extra\s+text|justification)\b",
    r"\bdo\s+not\s+(?:explain|include|add|provide\s+context)\b",
]

_SHORT_ANSWER_REQUEST_RE = re.compile(
    "|".join(_SHORT_ANSWER_REQUEST_PATTERNS), re.IGNORECASE
)

# Explanatory glue that is not part of a bare short answer.
_EXPLANATORY_GLUE_PATTERNS = [
    r"\balso\s+known\s+as\b",
    r"\baka\b",
    r"\bwhich\s+is\b",
    r"\bbecause\b",
    r"\bsuch\s+as\b",
    r"\bfor\s+example\b",
    r"\be\.g\.",
    r"\bi\.e\.",
    r"\bthat\s+is\b",
    r"\b(?:the|my|our)\s+answer\s+is\b",
    r"\b(?:the\s+)?correct\s+answer\s+is\b",
    r"\bin\s+other\s+words\b",
    r"\bstands\s+for\b",
    r"\brefers\s+to\b",
    r"\bknown\s+as\b",
    r"\blocated\s+in\b",
    r"\b(?:the\s+)?(?:show|movie|film|series|book|play|title|cast|character|actor|actress)\s+(?:is|was)\b",
    r"\bincludes?\b",
    r"\bconsists?\s+of\b",
    r"\bcontains?\b",
    r"\b(?:played\s+by|directed\s+by|starring|role\s+of)\b",
    r"\bis\s+a\s+(?:type|kind|species|member|part|form)\s+of\b",
]

_EXPLANATORY_GLUE_RE = re.compile(
    "|".join(_EXPLANATORY_GLUE_PATTERNS), re.IGNORECASE
)

_MARKDOWN_EMPHASIS_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<!\w)(\*|_){1,3}[^*_\n]+(\1){1,3}(?!\w)"
)

_MARKDOWN_LINK_RE = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]+\]\([^)]*\)")

_MARKDOWN_CODE_RE = re.compile(r"`[^`]+`")

# A bare short answer wrapped only in a Markdown emphasis layer such as
# ``**bumpkin**``, ``*omelet*``, or ``__eagle__`` is still the bare answer.
# Strip that single surrounding layer before applying the formatting checks;
# emphasis that is embedded in a larger explanatory construction is left in
# place so the surrounding material is still detected.
_SURROUNDING_MARKDOWN_EMPHASIS_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(\*{1,3}|_{1,3})(.+?)\1\s*$", re.DOTALL
)

_PARENTHETICAL_RE = re.compile(r"\([^)]*\)")

_EM_DASH_RE = re.compile(r"[—–]")

_SEMICOLON_RE = re.compile(r";")

_MULTILINE_OR_TAB_RE = re.compile(r"[\n\t]")

_BLOCKQUOTE_OR_LIST_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:>|[-*+]\s+|\d+[.)]\s+)", re.MULTILINE)

# Leading pronoun/copula lead-ins such as "It is Paris" are full-sentence
# answers, not bare short answers.  The copula alternatives are lower-case so
# title-case titles such as "This Is Spinal Tap" are preserved.
_LEADING_PRONOUN_COPULA_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:[Ii]t|[Hh]e|[Ss]he|[Tt]hey|[Tt]here|[Hh]ere|[Tt]his|[Tt]hat)\s+(?:is|was|are|were)\b"
)

# Cast/description vocabulary that indicates an answer mode other than a bare
# entity when it appears in a longer phrase.
_CAST_DESCRIPTION_WORDS_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:cast|characters?|actors?|actresses?|starring|played\s+by|directed\s+by|role\s+of)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

# Trailing prepositional qualifiers/attributions are not part of a bare short
# answer.  Keep the preposition lowercase so title-case phrases such as
# "Stand By Me" are not treated as an attribution.
_TRAILING_PREPOSITION_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:in|at|on|from|near|by)\s+[A-Z][\w.'’\-]*(?:\s+[A-Z][\w.'’\-]*)*\.?\s*$"
)

# Comma-separated capitalized elaboration such as "Dahlonega, Georgia".
# Common abbreviation suffixes are allowed because they are part of the
# answer itself (for example "Washington, D.C." or "Martin Luther King, Jr.").
_COMMA_ELABORATION_ABBREVIATIONS = {
    "d.c.",
    "jr.",
    "sr.",
    "inc.",
    "ltd.",
    "co.",
    "st.",
    "mt.",
    "dr.",
    "mr.",
    "mrs.",
    "ms.",
    "u.s.",
    "u.s.a.",
    "u.k.",
}

_COMMA_CAPITALIZED_QUALIFIER_RE = re.compile(
    r"[A-Z][\w.'’\-]*(?:\s+[A-Z][\w.'’\-]*)*\.?$"
)

def _requests_short_answer(user_text):
    return bool(_SHORT_ANSWER_REQUEST_RE.search(user_text))


def _strip_surrounding_markdown_emphasis(text):
    """Remove one Markdown emphasis layer that wraps the whole answer.

    ``**bumpkin**``, ``*omelet*``, and ``__eagle__`` are bare answers with an
    emphasis wrapper, not explanatory formatting, so the wrapper is removed
    before the short-answer checks run.  Emphasis that is only part of a larger
    construction (for example ``**True** — ...``) is left intact so the extra
    material can still be detected.
    """
    match = _SURROUNDING_MARKDOWN_EMPHASIS_RE.match(text)
    if not match:
        return text
    return match.group(2).strip()


# Bare boolean/yes-no answer detection.  A short-answer prompt that is not a
# yes/no or true/false question cannot have "True", "False", "Yes", or "No"
# as its bare answer, so block those completions rather than accepting them.
_BARE_BOOLEAN_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:true|false|yes|no)\s*[.!?]?\s*$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

_BOOLEAN_QUESTION_MARKER_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:"
    r"true\s+or\s+false|false\s+or\s+true|"
    r"yes\s+or\s+no|no\s+or\s+yes|"
    r"yes\s*/\s*no|no\s*/\s*yes|"
    r"true\s*/\s*false|false\s*/\s*true|"
    r"yes-no|no-yes|true-false|false-true"
    r")\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

_YES_NO_AUX_START_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:is|are|am|do|does|did|can|could|will|would|should|shall|has|have|had|may|might|must)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _is_bare_boolean_answer(assistant_text):
    """True when the final answer is only a bare boolean/yes-no token.

    A surrounding Markdown emphasis layer (``**True**``) and matching quotes
    (``"yes"``) are ignored, as is a single trailing sentence-ending
    punctuation mark, because those are still bare boolean tokens.  Anchoring
    the token to the whole answer means longer answers that merely contain
    ``yes`` or ``no`` are not affected.
    """
    text = _strip_surrounding_markdown_emphasis(assistant_text).strip()
    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == text[-1] and text[0] in ('"', "'", "`"):
        text = text[1:-1].strip()
    return bool(_BARE_BOOLEAN_TOKEN_RE.match(text))


def _contains_yes_no_question_sentence(sentence):
    """True when a text segment is a direct yes/no question."""
    sentence = sentence.strip()
    candidates = [sentence]
    # Allow labels such as "Question: Is ...?"
    candidates.extend(re.split(r"[:：]\s*", sentence))
    for candidate in candidates:
        candidate = candidate.strip()
        if candidate.endswith("?") and _YES_NO_AUX_START_RE.match(candidate):
            return True
    return False


def _is_boolean_question(user_text):
    """True when the prompt asks a yes/no or true/false question."""
    if _BOOLEAN_QUESTION_MARKER_RE.search(user_text):
        return True

    for segment in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", user_text):
        if _contains_yes_no_question_sentence(segment):
            return True
    return False


def _has_trailing_prepositional_qualifier(assistant_text):
    """True when the answer ends with a prepositional qualifier/attribution."""
    return bool(_TRAILING_PREPOSITION_RE.search(assistant_text))


def _is_geographic_qualifier(suffix):
    """True when a comma suffix is a known state/province/country name."""
    normalized = suffix.strip()
    normalized = re.sub(r"\.\s*$", "", normalized)
    normalized = normalized.lower().replace("’", "'")
    return normalized in _GEOGRAPHIC_QUALIFIERS


def _is_multiword_proper_noun_core(prefix):
    """True when the text before the comma is a capitalized proper-noun phrase."""
    if not re.search(r"\s", prefix):
        return False
    return bool(_COMMA_CAPITALIZED_QUALIFIER_RE.match(prefix))


def _has_comma_capitalized_elaboration(assistant_text):
    """True when an answer appends a capitalized qualifier after a comma.

    The classic single-word shape ``<Answer>, <Capitalized Qualifier>`` is
    always rejected (for example ``Dahlonega, Georgia``).  The same check also
    applies to a multi-word proper-noun answer core when the suffix is a
    geographic qualifier, such as ``Salt Lake City, Utah`` or
    ``Buenos Aires, Argentina``.  A comma inside a multi-word title/name such
    as ``Welcome Back, Kotter`` is part of the answer rather than an appended
    qualifier, so it is not flagged.  Common abbreviations such as ``D.C.``,
    ``Jr.``, and ``Sr.`` remain exempt.
    """
    for match in re.finditer(r",\s*", assistant_text):
        prefix = assistant_text[:match.start()].strip()
        suffix = assistant_text[match.end():].strip()
        if not prefix or not suffix:
            continue

        if suffix.lower() in _COMMA_ELABORATION_ABBREVIATIONS:
            continue

        suffix_is_capitalized = bool(_COMMA_CAPITALIZED_QUALIFIER_RE.match(suffix))
        suffix_is_geographic = _is_geographic_qualifier(suffix)
        if not suffix_is_capitalized and not suffix_is_geographic:
            continue

        # The original single-word answer core shape.
        if not re.search(r"\s", prefix):
            return True

        # A multi-word answer core is only an elaboration when it is followed
        # by a geographic qualifier (state/province/country); otherwise the
        # comma is treated as part of the answer title/name.
        if suffix_is_geographic and _is_multiword_proper_noun_core(prefix):
            return True

    return False


# Leading question-phrase answer formats such as "What is a well?" are full
# Jeopardy-style sentences rather than the requested bare answer.  Keep the
# auxiliary verb lower-case and require the answer object to start with a
# lower-case common noun (or an article) so title-case question titles such as
# "Who Framed Roger Rabbit" are not treated as violations.
_LEADING_QUESTION_ANSWER_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*"
    r"(?:"
    r"(?:[Ww]hat|[Ww]ho|[Ww]here|[Ww]hen|[Ww]hy|[Ww]hich)"
    r"(?:'s|’s|\s+is\b|\s+are\b|\s+was\b|\s+were\b)"
    r"|"
    r"(?:[Hh]ow)\s+(?:many|much|old|long|far|tall|big|often)\b"
    r")"
    r"\s+(?:(?:[Aa]n?|[Tt]he)\s+)?[a-z][\w’'\-]*"
)

# Full-sentence definitional answers for short-answer prompts, e.g.
# "A campaign slogan for William Henry Harrison and John Tyler in the 1840
# U.S. presidential election." or "A community in Maryland".  These start with
# an article, a generic category noun, and a definitional preposition, which is
# not a bare short answer.
_DEFINITIONAL_CATEGORY_NOUN_PATTERN = (
    r"(?:"
    r"campaign\s+slogan|slogan|community|census-designated\s+place|"
    r"term|word|phrase|name|title|concept|idea|theory|method|process|technique|"
    r"city|town|state|country|region|person|character|"
    r"film|movie|novel|book|song|album|play|painting|work|device|tool|instrument|"
    r"system|disease|condition|event|war|battle|treaty|law|amendment|period|era|"
    r"epoch|language|religion|movement|organization|organisation|company|brand|"
    r"type|kind|species|form|class|genre|group|team|party|member|part|role|job|"
    r"position|office"
    r")"
)

_FULL_SENTENCE_DEFINITION_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:[Aa]n?|[Tt]he)\s+"
    + _DEFINITIONAL_CATEGORY_NOUN_PATTERN
    + r"(?:\s+[a-z][\w’'\-]*){0,2}\s+"
    + r"(?:for|in|of|by|about|that|which|used\s+(?:for|in|to)|referring\s+to)\b"
)

# An indefinite article plus a three-or-more-word lowercase descriptive
# common-noun phrase is a full noun-phrase description, not a bare short answer
# (e.g. "A hot air balloon" or "A giant flour tortilla").  Article + one- or
# two-word phrases such as "A subject" or "A eucalyptus tree" remain valid,
# as do title-case titles such as "The Stand" or "The Bastille".
_INDEFINITE_ARTICLE_DESCRIPTIVE_PHRASE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*[Aa]n?\s+[a-z][\w’'\-]*(?:\s+[a-z][\w’'\-]*){2,}\.?\s*$"
)

# A descriptive common-noun phrase headed by a rank, ordinal, or superlative
# modifier and followed by a prepositional complement is a short description
# rather than a bare answer (e.g. "Second largest city in Germany" or
# "Largest city in France").  The head is case-insensitive so the normal
# sentence-initial capital is accepted, but the descriptive words between the
# head and the preposition must be lower-case.  A bare title such as
# "Last Tango in Paris" keeps its inner words capitalized and is not matched.
_RANK_SUPERLATIVE_DESCRIPTIVE_PHRASE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*"
    r"(?i:"
    r"first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth|seventh|eighth|ninth|tenth|"
    r"eleventh|twelfth|thirteenth|fourteenth|fifteenth|sixteenth|"
    r"seventeenth|eighteenth|nineteenth|twentieth|"
    r"last|next|"
    r"largest|smallest|tallest|biggest|highest|lowest|oldest|newest|"
    r"longest|shortest|best|worst|top|leading|chief|main|"
    r"most\s+[a-z]+|least\s+[a-z]+"
    r")"
    r"(?:\s+[a-z][\w’'\-]*)+?\s+"
    r"(?:in|of|on|by|near|at|to)\b"
)

# Parenthetical asides that elaborate an otherwise short answer.  This hint
# regex detects explicit aside markers inside a parenthetical (years, roles,
# and "also called"/aka glosses). Plain alternate-name parentheticals are
# caught by _has_parenthetical_aside when they follow an existing answer core.
_PARENTHETICAL_ASIDE_HINT_RE = re.compile(
    r"\([^)]*(?:\b(?:also\s+(?:known\s+as|called)|aka|a\.k\.a\.)\b|"
    r"\b(?:19|20)\d{2}\b|"
    r"\b(?:director|producer|actor|actress|starring|played\s+by|released\s+in|"
    r"published\s+in|originally|based\s+on|circa|est\.)\b)[^)]*\)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _has_leading_question_phrase(assistant_text):
    """True when the final answer is a Jeopardy-style question sentence."""
    return bool(_LEADING_QUESTION_ANSWER_RE.search(assistant_text))


def _has_full_sentence_definition(assistant_text):
    """True when the final answer is a definitional full sentence/description."""
    return bool(_FULL_SENTENCE_DEFINITION_RE.match(assistant_text))


def _has_indefinite_article_descriptive_phrase(assistant_text):
    """True for an indefinite-article-prefixed descriptive noun phrase.

    The phrase must have at least three lower-case content words after the
    article.  One- and two-word article phrases are deliberately left alone
    because some valid short answers take that form (for example
    ``A subject`` and ``A eucalyptus tree``).
    """
    return bool(_INDEFINITE_ARTICLE_DESCRIPTIVE_PHRASE_RE.match(assistant_text))


def _has_rank_superlative_descriptive_phrase(assistant_text):
    """True for a rank/ordinal/superlative-headed descriptive phrase."""
    return bool(_RANK_SUPERLATIVE_DESCRIPTIVE_PHRASE_RE.match(assistant_text))


def _has_parenthetical_aside(assistant_text):
    """True when the answer contains a parenthesized elaboration.

    A leading parenthesized token can be an integral part of the answer
    (for example ``(Lou) Gehrig``), so it is allowed as long as it does not
    itself contain aside material such as a year, role, or "also called"
    gloss. Parentheticals that follow an existing answer core, or that are the
    entire answer, are still treated as explanatory asides.
    """
    for match in _PARENTHETICAL_RE.finditer(assistant_text):
        parenthetical = match.group(0)
        if _PARENTHETICAL_ASIDE_HINT_RE.search(parenthetical):
            return True
        prefix = assistant_text[:match.start()].strip()
        suffix = assistant_text[match.end():].strip()
        if prefix:
            return True
        if not suffix:
            return True
    return False


def _has_leading_pronoun_copula(assistant_text):
    """True when the answer is a pronoun-plus-copula full sentence."""
    return bool(_LEADING_PRONOUN_COPULA_RE.match(assistant_text))


def _has_non_entity_description(assistant_text):
    """True for comma-separated lists and cast/description answer modes.

    This merges the final-answer heuristics that used to live in the
    tool-interaction hook into the completion hook.  A bare short answer should
    not be a two-or-more-comma list, and a longer phrase that explicitly
    mentions cast/characters/actors/starring is an explanation rather than the
    requested entity.
    """
    text = _strip_surrounding_markdown_emphasis(assistant_text).strip()
    word_count = len(text.split())
    if word_count >= 4 and text.count(",") >= 2:
        return True
    if word_count >= 4 and _CAST_DESCRIPTION_WORDS_RE.search(text):
        return True
    return False


def _has_explanatory_formatting(assistant_text):
    """Return True when the final answer is more than the bare short answer."""
    text = _strip_surrounding_markdown_emphasis(assistant_text)
    if _MARKDOWN_EMPHASIS_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _MARKDOWN_LINK_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _MARKDOWN_CODE_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _has_parenthetical_aside(text):
        return True
    if _EM_DASH_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _SEMICOLON_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _MULTILINE_OR_TAB_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _BLOCKQUOTE_OR_LIST_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _has_non_entity_description(text):
        return True
    if _has_leading_pronoun_copula(text):
        return True
    if _EXPLANATORY_GLUE_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _has_trailing_prepositional_qualifier(text):
        return True
    if _has_comma_capitalized_elaboration(text):
        return True
    if _has_leading_question_phrase(text):
        return True
    if _has_full_sentence_definition(text):
        return True
    if _has_indefinite_article_descriptive_phrase(text):
        return True
    if _has_rank_superlative_descriptive_phrase(text):
        return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main hook
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def decide(event):
    if not isinstance(event, dict):
        return _allow()

    if event.get("stop_hook_active") is False:
        return _allow()

    transcript_path = event.get("transcript_path")
    records = _load_records(transcript_path)
    if not records:
        return _allow()

    messages = _collect_messages(records)
    if not messages:
        return _allow()

    # Find the latest real user instruction (tool-result user turns are already
    # skipped) and the latest assistant turn, even if that turn has no text.
    user_text = ""
    for role, text in reversed(messages):
        if role == "user" and text:
            user_text = text
            break

    assistant_text = None
    for role, text in reversed(messages):
        if role == "assistant":
            assistant_text = text
            break

    if not user_text or not assistant_text:
        return _allow()

    if not _requests_short_answer(user_text):
        return _allow()

    if not _is_boolean_question(user_text) and _is_bare_boolean_answer(assistant_text):
        return _block(
            "The user requested a short/bare answer but did not ask a yes/no or "
            "true/false question, so a bare boolean/yes-no token such as "
            "'true', 'false', 'yes', or 'no' cannot be the requested short "
            "answer. Return only the short answer the prompt asks for, with "
            "no extra text, explanation, or formatting."
        )

    if not _has_explanatory_formatting(assistant_text):
        return _allow()

    return _block(
        "The user requested a short/bare answer, but the final response is not "
        "bare. It may be phrased as a leading question (for example 'What is a "
        "well?'), as a full-sentence definition (for example 'A campaign "
        "slogan for ...'), as an article-prefixed descriptive phrase (for "
        "example 'A hot air balloon'), as a rank/ordinal/superlative "
        "descriptive phrase (for example 'Second largest city in Germany'), "
        "or with explanatory formatting/asides such as markdown emphasis "
        "attached to extra explanation, parenthesized alternate "
        "titles/years/roles/'also called' glosses, em-dashes, explanatory "
        "glue, semicolon-separated explanations, multi-line/tab-separated "
        "text, leading pronoun/copula sentences such as 'It is Paris', "
        "comma-separated lists or cast/description phrases, trailing "
        "prepositional qualifiers such as 'by R.E.M.', or comma-separated "
        "elaborations such as 'Dahlonega, Georgia' or 'Salt Lake City, "
        "Utah'. Return only the bare short answer with no question phrasing, "
        "definitions, descriptive phrases, explanatory markdown, parentheses, "
        "em-dashes, semicolons, multi-line text, explanations, lists, "
        "attributions, or extra qualifiers."
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        event = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError):
        event = {}
    print(json.dumps(decide(event)))

import json
import re
import sys


_BAD_ANSWER_FEEDBACK = (
    "Return only the requested short entity from the context; "
    "no yes/no, explanation, cast list, or title."
)

_BINARY_ANSWERS = {"yes", "no", "true", "false"}

_STRONG_SENTENCE_STARTERS = (
    "the answer is",
    "the correct answer is",
    "answer is",
    "the answer",
    "the correct answer",
    "the solution is",
    "the entity is",
    "it is",
    "this is",
    "that is",
    "there is",
    "there are",
    "here is",
    "he is",
    "she is",
    "it was",
    "he was",
    "she was",
    "they are",
    "they were",
    "the show is",
    "the show was",
    "the movie is",
    "the movie was",
    "the film is",
    "the film was",
    "the series is",
    "the series was",
    "the book is",
    "the book was",
    "the play is",
    "the play was",
    "the title is",
    "the cast is",
    "the character is",
    "the actor is",
    "the actress is",
    "i think",
    "i believe",
)


def _strip_markdown(text):
    """Remove common Markdown wrappers from a short answer string."""
    cleaned = text.strip()

    # Fenced code blocks.
    if cleaned.startswith("```"):
        cleaned = re.sub(r"^```[^\n]*\n?", "", cleaned)
        cleaned = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", cleaned)

    # Leading heading/list markers.
    cleaned = re.sub(r"^\s*(?:#{1,6}\s*|>\s*|[-*+]\s+|\d+[.)]\s+)", "", cleaned)

    # Markdown links/images, keeping only the visible label.
    cleaned = re.sub(r"!\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", cleaned)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", cleaned)

    # Inline Markdown emphasis/code markers, whether or not they wrap the
    # entire candidate.
    cleaned = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]+)\*\*", r"\1", cleaned)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"__([^_]+)__", r"\1", cleaned)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"\*([^*]+)\*", r"\1", cleaned)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"(?<!\w)_([^_]+)_(?!\w)", r"\1", cleaned)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"`([^`]+)`", r"\1", cleaned)

    # Stray emphasis/code characters on the ends.
    cleaned = cleaned.strip("*_`")

    return cleaned.strip()


def _strip_outer_punctuation(text):
    """Remove balanced outer quotes/brackets, then leading/trailing punctuation."""
    cleaned = text.strip()
    pairs = [("(", ")"), ("[", "]"), ("{", "}"), ('"', '"'), ("'", "'")]
    changed = True
    while changed and len(cleaned) >= 2:
        changed = False
        for left, right in pairs:
            if cleaned.startswith(left) and cleaned.endswith(right):
                cleaned = cleaned[1:-1].strip()
                changed = True
                break

    # Strip loose sentence/quote punctuation from the ends only. Unpaired
    # closing brackets are left alone here so trailing parentheticals can be
    # handled separately.
    cleaned = cleaned.strip("\"'.,;:!?")
    return cleaned.strip()


def _strip_trailing_parentheticals(text):
    """Remove trailing parenthetical/bracketed qualifiers such as (born 1936)."""
    cleaned = text.strip()
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for pattern in (r"\s+\([^()]*\)\s*$", r"\s+\[[^\[\]]*\]\s*$"):
            new = re.sub(pattern, "", cleaned)
            if new != cleaned:
                cleaned = new.strip()
                changed = True
                break
    return cleaned.strip()


def clean_candidate(text):
    """Normalize a raw final-answer candidate to a bare short-entity form."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return ""
    cleaned = _strip_markdown(text)
    cleaned = _strip_outer_punctuation(cleaned)
    cleaned = _strip_trailing_parentheticals(cleaned)
    return cleaned.strip()


def _is_full_sentence(text):
    """Heuristic for full-sentence explanations instead of a bare entity."""
    cleaned = text.strip()
    words = cleaned.split()
    word_count = len(words)

    if word_count <= 2:
        return False

    # Internal sentence punctuation followed by a capital letter implies prose.
    if re.search(r"[.!?][\"')\]]?\s+[A-Z0-9]", cleaned):
        return True

    lowered = cleaned.lower()
    if lowered.startswith(_STRONG_SENTENCE_STARTERS):
        return True

    # Common copula/auxiliary verbs are a strong signal at this length.
    if re.search(r"\b(?:is|are|was|were|am)\b", lowered):
        return True
    if re.search(r"\b(?:has|have|had)\b", lowered):
        return True
    if re.search(r"\b(?:refers to|means|indicates|shows|denotes|represents)\b", lowered):
        return True
    if re.search(r"\b(?:includes|include|consists of|contains|contain)\b", lowered):
        return True
    if re.search(
        r"\b(?:played|plays|portrayed|portrays|starred|stars|features|featured|"
        r"directed|directs|wrote|writes|created|creates|served as|became|become)\b",
        lowered,
    ):
        return True

    return False


def _is_description_or_list(text):
    """Heuristic for titles/cast lists/descriptions instead of a short entity."""
    cleaned = text.strip()
    lowered = cleaned.lower()
    word_count = len(cleaned.split())

    if not cleaned:
        return True

    # Lists and multi-line prose are not short entities.
    if "\n" in cleaned or "\t" in cleaned:
        return True
    if re.search(r"^\s*(?:[-*+]\s+|\d+[.)]\s+)", cleaned):
        return True
    if cleaned.count(",") >= 2 and word_count >= 4:
        return True
    if word_count > 10:
        return True

    # A colon plus trailing explanation is prose, not a short answer.
    if ":" in cleaned and word_count >= 5:
        return True

    # Explicit cast/character/description vocabulary is a different answer mode.
    if word_count >= 4 and re.search(
        r"\b(?:cast|character|characters|actor|actors|actress|actresses|"
        r"director|directed by|played by|starring|role of|episode|plot|premise)\b",
        lowered,
    ):
        return True

    return False


def _is_bad_candidate(cleaned):
    """Return True when the candidate is not a bare requested entity."""
    if not cleaned:
        return True
    lowered = cleaned.lower()
    if lowered in _BINARY_ANSWERS:
        return True
    if _is_full_sentence(cleaned):
        return True
    if _is_description_or_list(cleaned):
        return True
    return False


def before_final(candidate):
    """Stop-hook decision for the final answer candidate.

    Clean short entities are returned as replacements. Other answer modes
    (yes/no, true/false, explanations, cast lists, descriptions) are left
    untouched so the model can be prompted to return the short entity instead.
    """
    cleaned = clean_candidate(candidate)
    if _is_bad_candidate(cleaned):
        return {"action": "continue", "feedback": _BAD_ANSWER_FEEDBACK}
    return {"action": "replace", "answer": cleaned}


def _extract_candidate(event):
    """Find a final-answer candidate string in a Stop-hook event payload."""
    if not isinstance(event, dict):
        return None

    candidate_keys = (
        "answer",
        "candidate",
        "final_answer",
        "final_response",
        "response",
        "output",
        "text",
        "content",
        "message",
        "value",
    )
    for key in candidate_keys:
        value = event.get(key)
        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
            return value
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            found = _extract_candidate(value)
            if found is not None:
                return found
        if isinstance(value, list):
            for item in value:
                if isinstance(item, str) and item.strip():
                    return item
                if isinstance(item, dict):
                    found = _extract_candidate(item)
                    if found is not None:
                        return found

    stop = event.get("stop")
    if isinstance(stop, dict):
        found = _extract_candidate(stop)
        if found is not None:
            return found

    return None


def decide(event):
    # Initial tool hook behavior stays unchanged for PreToolUse/PostToolUse.
    if not isinstance(event, dict):
        return {}

    hook_event_name = event.get("hook_event_name")

    if hook_event_name == "Stop" and event.get("stop_hook_active") is True:
        candidate = _extract_candidate(event)
        if candidate is None:
            # A Stop hook must allow Claude to exit when no candidate is
            # available; continue is the permissive Stop-hook action.
            return {"action": "continue"}
        return before_final(candidate)

    return {}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    event = json.load(sys.stdin)
    print(json.dumps(decide(event)))

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path


# Stop-hook decision helpers.  Keep the hook protocol payload unchanged:
# the Stop hook always receives a JSON event on stdin and must print a
# single JSON decision object on stdout.
def _allow():
    return {"decision": {"decision": "allow"}}


def _block(reason):
    return {"decision": {"decision": "block", "reason": reason}}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Transcript loading / message extraction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _load_records(transcript_path):
    """Read a Claude transcript file.

    Transcripts are normally JSONL, but accept a top-level JSON array as well.
    Return a list of record dicts, or [] when the file is missing/invalid.
    """
    if not transcript_path:
        return []

    path = Path(transcript_path)
    try:
        raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except OSError:
        return []

    # Support whole-file JSON exports (a top-level array, or an object with a
    # "messages"/"transcript" array) in addition to JSONL.
    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
        if isinstance(data, list):
            return [item for item in data if isinstance(item, dict)]
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            for key in ("messages", "transcript"):
                items = data.get(key)
                if isinstance(items, list):
                    return [item for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        pass

    records = []
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            record = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if isinstance(record, dict):
            records.append(record)
    return records


def _extract_text(content):
    """Best-effort extraction of plain text from a transcript content value."""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content

    if isinstance(content, list):
        parts = []
        for block in content:
            if isinstance(block, str):
                parts.append(block)
            elif isinstance(block, dict):
                if block.get("type") == "text" and isinstance(block.get("text"), str):
                    parts.append(block["text"])
                elif isinstance(block.get("text"), str):
                    parts.append(block["text"])
        return "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)

    if isinstance(content, dict):
        return _extract_text(content.get("content", ""))

    return ""


def _is_tool_result_message(record):
    """True when a user-role record is only carrying tool results."""
    message = record.get("message") if isinstance(record, dict) else None
    content = message.get("content") if isinstance(message, dict) else record.get("content")
    if isinstance(content, list) and content:
        return all(
            isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_result"
            for block in content
        )
    return False


def _message_role(record):
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return None

    top_type = record.get("type")
    if top_type in ("user", "assistant"):
        return top_type

    message = record.get("message")
    if isinstance(message, dict):
        role = message.get("role")
        if role in ("user", "assistant"):
            return role

    role = record.get("role")
    if role in ("user", "assistant"):
        return role

    return None


def _message_content(record):
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return ""
    message = record.get("message")
    if isinstance(message, dict):
        content = message.get("content")
        if content is not None:
            return content
    return record.get("content", "")


def _collect_messages(records):
    """Return [(role, text), ...] for user/assistant messages.

    Tool-result user turns are skipped because they are not real user
    instructions.  Assistant turns are kept even when they have no text so the
    caller can tell whether the *last* assistant turn actually contains a
    final text answer.
    """
    messages = []
    for record in records:
        role = _message_role(record)
        if role not in ("user", "assistant"):
            continue
        if role == "user" and _is_tool_result_message(record):
            continue
        text = _extract_text(_message_content(record)).strip()
        messages.append((role, text))
    return messages


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Formatting detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SHORT_ANSWER_REQUEST_PATTERNS = [
    r"\b(?:short|bare|one-word|single-word|brief|concise|direct)\s+(?:answer|response|reply|format)\b",
    r"\b(?:answer|respond|reply)\s+(?:with|using|in)?\s*(?:only|just|nothing\s+but|no\s+more\s+than)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:short|bare|one-word|single-word|brief|concise|direct)?\s*(?:answer|response|reply|name|word|number|value)\b",
    r"\b(?:answer|respond|reply)\s+(?:only|just)\s+(?:with\s+)?(?:the\s+)?(?:short|bare|one-word|single-word|brief|concise|direct)?\s*(?:answer|response|reply|name|word|number|value)\b",
    r"\b(?:answer|respond|reply)\s+with\s+the\s+(?:name|word|number|short\s+answer|answer)\s+only\b",
    r"\b(?:only|just|nothing\s+but)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:short|bare|one-word|single-word|brief|concise|direct)?\s*(?:answer|name|word|number|value|response|reply)\b",
    r"\b(?:give|provide|return|state|say|tell\s+me)\s+(?:only|just)\s+the\b",
    r"\b(?:just|only)\s+(?:give|provide|return|state|say|tell\s+me)\s+the\b",
    r"\b(?:give|provide|return|state|say)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:name|word|number|short\s+answer|answer)\s+(?:only|just)\b",
    r"\b(?:only|just)\s+(?:one\s+)?(?:word|name|number)\b",
    r"\banswer\s+only\b",
    r"\banswer\s+in\s+one\s+word\b",
    r"\b(?:with|using)\s+(?:only|just)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:short|bare)?\s*(?:answer|name|word|number)\b",
    r"\bno\s+(?:explanation|commentary|extra|additional\s+text|justification)\b",
    r"\bwithout\s+(?:any\s+)?(?:explanation|commentary|markdown|formatting|extra\s+text|justification)\b",
    r"\bdo\s+not\s+(?:explain|include|add|provide\s+context)\b",
]

_SHORT_ANSWER_REQUEST_RE = re.compile(
    "|".join(_SHORT_ANSWER_REQUEST_PATTERNS), re.IGNORECASE
)

# Explanatory glue that is not part of a bare short answer.
_EXPLANATORY_GLUE_PATTERNS = [
    r"\balso\s+known\s+as\b",
    r"\baka\b",
    r"\bwhich\s+is\b",
    r"\bbecause\b",
    r"\bsuch\s+as\b",
    r"\bfor\s+example\b",
    r"\be\.g\.",
    r"\bi\.e\.",
    r"\bthat\s+is\b",
    r"\b(?:the|my|our)\s+answer\s+is\b",
    r"\b(?:the\s+)?correct\s+answer\s+is\b",
    r"\bin\s+other\s+words\b",
    r"\bstands\s+for\b",
    r"\brefers\s+to\b",
    r"\bknown\s+as\b",
    r"\blocated\s+in\b",
    r"\bis\s+a\s+(?:type|kind|species|member|part|form)\s+of\b",
]

_EXPLANATORY_GLUE_RE = re.compile(
    "|".join(_EXPLANATORY_GLUE_PATTERNS), re.IGNORECASE
)

_MARKDOWN_EMPHASIS_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<!\w)(\*|_){1,3}[^*_\n]+(\1){1,3}(?!\w)"
)

_MARKDOWN_LINK_RE = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]+\]\([^)]*\)")

_MARKDOWN_CODE_RE = re.compile(r"`[^`]+`")

# A bare short answer wrapped only in a Markdown emphasis layer such as
# ``**bumpkin**``, ``*omelet*``, or ``__eagle__`` is still the bare answer.
# Strip that single surrounding layer before applying the formatting checks;
# emphasis that is embedded in a larger explanatory construction is left in
# place so the surrounding material is still detected.
_SURROUNDING_MARKDOWN_EMPHASIS_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(\*{1,3}|_{1,3})(.+?)\1\s*$", re.DOTALL
)

# Similarly, a bare answer wrapped only in a Markdown code span (for example
# `` `eagle` `` or ````code````) is the bare answer and can be normalized
# before the formatting checks run.
_SURROUNDING_MARKDOWN_CODE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(`{1,3})([^`\n]+?)\1\s*$"
)

_PARENTHETICAL_RE = re.compile(r"\([^)]*\)")

_EM_DASH_RE = re.compile(r"[—–]")

_DOUBLE_HYPHEN_ASIDE_RE = re.compile(r"\s--\s")

# Slash-separated alternatives are handled by
# _has_slash_separated_alternatives below.  The detection is intentionally
# conservative: fractions/dates, all-caps slash names such as "AC/DC", and
# units/abbreviations such as "km/h" are not alternatives.

_BLOCKQUOTE_OR_LIST_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:>|[-*+]\s+|\d+[.)]\s+)", re.MULTILINE)

# Trailing prepositional qualifiers/attributions are not part of a bare short
# answer.  Keep the preposition lowercase so title-case phrases such as
# "Stand By Me" are not treated as an attribution.
_TRAILING_PREPOSITION_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:in|at|on|from|near|by)\s+[A-Z][\w.'’\-]*(?:\s+[A-Z][\w.'’\-]*)*\.?\s*$"
)

# Comma-separated capitalized elaboration such as "Dahlonega, Georgia".
# Common abbreviation suffixes are allowed because they are part of the
# answer itself (for example "Washington, D.C." or "Martin Luther King, Jr.").
# NOTE: this syntactic check is intentionally disabled for short-answer
# formatting decisions because a two-part capitalized proper-noun pair such as
# "Anchorage, Alaska" is a legitimate bare answer.  Explanatory comma suffixes
# are still caught by the general explanatory-glue/aside checks when they
# contain explicit explanatory wording.
_COMMA_ELABORATION_ABBREVIATIONS = {
    "d.c.",
    "jr.",
    "sr.",
    "inc.",
    "ltd.",
    "co.",
    "st.",
    "mt.",
    "dr.",
    "mr.",
    "mrs.",
    "ms.",
    "u.s.",
    "u.s.a.",
    "u.k.",
}

_COMMA_CAPITALIZED_QUALIFIER_RE = re.compile(
    r"[A-Z][\w.'’\-]*(?:\s+[A-Z][\w.'’\-]*)*\.?$"
)


def _requests_short_answer(user_text):
    return bool(_SHORT_ANSWER_REQUEST_RE.search(user_text))


def _strip_surrounding_markdown_emphasis(text):
    """Remove simple surrounding Markdown emphasis/code wrappers.

    ``**bumpkin**``, ``*omelet*``, ``__eagle__``, and `` `eagle` `` are bare
    answers with a Markdown wrapper, not explanatory formatting, so the wrapper
    is removed before the short-answer checks run.  Emphasis or code that is
    only part of a larger construction (for example ``**True** — ...``) is left
    intact so the extra material can still be detected.
    """
    while True:
        match = _SURROUNDING_MARKDOWN_EMPHASIS_RE.match(text)
        if match:
            text = match.group(2).strip()
            continue

        match = _SURROUNDING_MARKDOWN_CODE_RE.match(text)
        if match:
            text = match.group(2).strip()
            continue

        return text


def _has_trailing_prepositional_qualifier(assistant_text):
    """True when the answer ends with a prepositional qualifier/attribution."""
    return bool(_TRAILING_PREPOSITION_RE.search(assistant_text))


def _has_comma_capitalized_elaboration(assistant_text):
    """Return True for a comma-separated capitalized elaboration.

    This syntactic test was disabled for short-answer decisions because a
    single-word answer followed by a comma and a capitalized proper-noun
    qualifier can be an integral place/person name such as
    ``Anchorage, Alaska``, which is a legitimate bare answer.  The function is
    retained as a no-op for interface compatibility; explanatory comma suffixes
    are handled by the other formatting checks when they contain explicit
    explanatory wording.
    """
    return False


# Leading question-phrase answer formats such as "What is a well?" are full
# Jeopardy-style sentences rather than the requested bare answer.  Keep the
# auxiliary verb lower-case and require the answer object to start with a
# lower-case common noun (or an article) so title-case question titles such as
# "Who Framed Roger Rabbit" are not treated as violations.
_LEADING_QUESTION_ANSWER_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*"
    r"(?:"
    r"(?:[Ww]hat|[Ww]ho|[Ww]here|[Ww]hen|[Ww]hy|[Ww]hich)"
    r"(?:'s|’s|\s+is\b|\s+are\b|\s+was\b|\s+were\b)"
    r"|"
    r"(?:[Hh]ow)\s+(?:many|much|old|long|far|tall|big|often)\b"
    r")"
    r"\s+(?:(?:[Aa]n?|[Tt]he)\s+)?[a-z][\w’'\-]*"
)

# Full-sentence definitional answers for short-answer prompts, e.g.
# "A campaign slogan for William Henry Harrison and John Tyler in the 1840
# U.S. presidential election." or "A community in Maryland".  These start with
# an article, a generic category noun, and a definitional preposition, which is
# not a bare short answer.
_DEFINITIONAL_CATEGORY_NOUN_PATTERN = (
    r"(?:"
    r"campaign\s+slogan|slogan|community|census-designated\s+place|"
    r"term|word|phrase|name|title|concept|idea|theory|method|process|technique|"
    r"city|town|state|country|region|person|character|"
    r"film|movie|novel|book|song|album|play|painting|work|device|tool|instrument|"
    r"system|disease|condition|event|war|battle|treaty|law|amendment|period|era|"
    r"epoch|language|religion|movement|organization|organisation|company|brand|"
    r"type|kind|species|form|class|genre|group|team|party|member|part|role|job|"
    r"position|office"
    r")"
)

_FULL_SENTENCE_DEFINITION_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:[Aa]n?|[Tt]he)\s+"
    + _DEFINITIONAL_CATEGORY_NOUN_PATTERN
    + r"(?:\s+[a-z][\w’'\-]*){0,2}\s+"
    + r"(?:for|in|of|by|about|that|which|used\s+(?:for|in|to)|referring\s+to)\b"
)

# An indefinite article plus a multi-word lowercase descriptive common-noun
# phrase is acceptable as a bare short answer when it stands alone (for example
# "a eucalyptus tree").  Only reject the phrase when it continues into an
# explanatory prepositional/relative clause, such as "a hot air balloon used
# for carrying people" or "a community in Maryland".
_INDEFINITE_ARTICLE_PHRASE_WITH_CLAUSE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*[Aa]n?\s+[a-z][\w’'\-]*(?:\s+[a-z][\w’'\-]*)+"
    r"(?:\s*,\s*|\s+)"
    r"(?:"
    r"that|which|who|whom|whose|where|when|"
    r"used\s+(?:for|in|to)|known\s+(?:for|as)|located\s+(?:in|at)|"
    r"found\s+(?:in|on)|referring\s+to|"
    r"for|in|of|by|about|as|to|with|from"
    r")\b"
)

# Parenthetical asides that elaborate an otherwise short answer.  This hint
# regex detects explicit aside markers inside a parenthetical (years, roles,
# and "also called"/aka glosses). Plain alternate-name parentheticals are
# caught by _has_parenthetical_aside when they follow an existing answer core.
_PARENTHETICAL_ASIDE_HINT_RE = re.compile(
    r"\([^)]*(?:\b(?:also\s+(?:known\s+as|called)|aka|a\.k\.a\.)\b|"
    r"\b(?:19|20)\d{2}\b|"
    r"\b(?:director|producer|actor|actress|starring|played\s+by|released\s+in|"
    r"published\s+in|originally|based\s+on|circa|est\.)\b)[^)]*\)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _has_leading_question_phrase(assistant_text):
    """True when the final answer is a Jeopardy-style question sentence."""
    return bool(_LEADING_QUESTION_ANSWER_RE.search(assistant_text))


def _has_full_sentence_definition(assistant_text):
    """True when the final answer is a definitional full sentence/description."""
    return bool(_FULL_SENTENCE_DEFINITION_RE.match(assistant_text))


def _has_indefinite_article_descriptive_phrase(assistant_text):
    """True for an article-prefixed descriptive phrase with a clause.

    A bare short answer may legitimately be an indefinite article plus a
    multi-word lower-case common-noun phrase (for example ``a eucalyptus
    tree``).  The answer is only rejected when that phrase continues into an
    explanatory prepositional/relative clause.
    """
    return bool(_INDEFINITE_ARTICLE_PHRASE_WITH_CLAUSE_RE.match(assistant_text))


def _has_parenthetical_aside(assistant_text):
    """True when the answer contains a parenthesized elaboration.

    A leading parenthesized token can be an integral part of the answer
    (for example ``(Lou) Gehrig``), so it is allowed as long as it does not
    itself contain aside material such as a year, role, or "also called"
    gloss. Parentheticals that follow an existing answer core, or that are the
    entire answer, are still treated as explanatory asides.
    """
    for match in _PARENTHETICAL_RE.finditer(assistant_text):
        parenthetical = match.group(0)
        if _PARENTHETICAL_ASIDE_HINT_RE.search(parenthetical):
            return True
        prefix = assistant_text[:match.start()].strip()
        suffix = assistant_text[match.end():].strip()
        if prefix:
            return True
        if not suffix:
            return True
    return False


def _has_double_hyphen_aside(assistant_text):
    """True when the answer contains a `` -- `` aside."""
    return bool(_DOUBLE_HYPHEN_ASIDE_RE.search(assistant_text))


def _is_vowel_word(word):
    """True when *word* contains at least one vowel (a rough pronounceability
    check used to separate word alternatives from units/abbreviations)."""
    return bool(re.search(r"[aeiou]", word, re.IGNORECASE))


def _has_slash_separated_alternatives(assistant_text):
    """True when the answer gives slash-separated alternatives.

    A slash surrounded by whitespace is a clear alternatives separator.  A
    tight slash is only treated as an alternative when both sides look like
    pronounceable words, which keeps all-caps names (``AC/DC``, ``TCP/IP``)
    and units/abbreviations (``km/h``, ``m/s``) from being falsely blocked.
    """
    for match in re.finditer(r"/", assistant_text):
        left_text = assistant_text[:match.start()]
        right_text = assistant_text[match.end():]

        left_match = re.search(r"([A-Za-z][\w.'’\-]*)\s*$", left_text)
        right_match = re.match(r"\s*([A-Za-z][\w.'’\-]*)", right_text)
        if not left_match or not right_match:
            continue

        left = left_match.group(1)
        right = right_match.group(1)
        if not left or not right:
            continue

        # Do not treat URL path separators as slash alternatives.
        if "://" in left_text:
            continue

        # Integral slash names/abbreviations such as AC/DC or TCP/IP are all
        # uppercase on both sides; they are a single name, not alternatives.
        if left.isupper() and right.isupper():
            continue

        # Both sides must look like words rather than units or abbreviations.
        # This still catches "red / green", "The Postman / Il Postino",
        # "red/green", and "he/she", but avoids "km/h", "m/s", and "kg/m3".
        if not _is_vowel_word(left) or not _is_vowel_word(right):
            continue

        # A slash with whitespace on either side is an explicit alternatives
        # separator ("red / green", "The Postman / Il Postino").
        if re.search(r"\s+$", left_text) or re.match(r"\s+", right_text):
            return True

        # Tight slashes need at least one side long enough to be a word rather
        # than a tiny abbreviation ("he/she" is fine, "w/e" is not).
        if len(left) < 3 and len(right) < 3:
            continue

        return True

    return False


def _has_explanatory_formatting(assistant_text):
    """Return True when the final answer is more than the bare short answer."""
    text = _strip_surrounding_markdown_emphasis(assistant_text)
    if _MARKDOWN_EMPHASIS_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _MARKDOWN_LINK_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _MARKDOWN_CODE_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _has_parenthetical_aside(text):
        return True
    if _EM_DASH_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _has_double_hyphen_aside(text):
        return True
    if _has_slash_separated_alternatives(text):
        return True
    if _BLOCKQUOTE_OR_LIST_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _EXPLANATORY_GLUE_RE.search(text):
        return True
    if _has_trailing_prepositional_qualifier(text):
        return True
    if _has_leading_question_phrase(text):
        return True
    if _has_full_sentence_definition(text):
        return True
    if _has_indefinite_article_descriptive_phrase(text):
        return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main hook
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def decide(event):
    if event.get("stop_hook_active") is False:
        return _allow()

    transcript_path = event.get("transcript_path")
    records = _load_records(transcript_path)
    if not records:
        return _allow()

    messages = _collect_messages(records)
    if not messages:
        return _allow()

    # Find the latest real user instruction (tool-result user turns are already
    # skipped) and the latest assistant turn, even if that turn has no text.
    user_text = ""
    for role, text in reversed(messages):
        if role == "user" and text:
            user_text = text
            break

    assistant_text = None
    for role, text in reversed(messages):
        if role == "assistant":
            assistant_text = text
            break

    if not user_text or not assistant_text:
        return _allow()

    if not _requests_short_answer(user_text):
        return _allow()

    if not _has_explanatory_formatting(assistant_text):
        return _allow()

    return _block(
        "The user requested a short/bare answer, but the final response is not "
        "bare. It may be phrased as a leading question (for example 'What is a "
        "well?'), as a full-sentence definition (for example 'A campaign "
        "slogan for ...'), as an article-prefixed descriptive phrase with an "
        "explanatory clause, or with explanatory formatting/asides such as "
        "markdown emphasis/code attached to extra explanation, parenthesized "
        "alternate titles/years/roles/'also called' glosses, em-dashes, "
        "double-hyphen asides, slash-separated alternatives, explanatory glue, "
        "or trailing prepositional qualifiers such as 'by R.E.M.'. Return only "
        "the bare short answer with no question phrasing, definitions, "
        "explanatory phrases, markdown, parentheses, dashes, alternatives, "
        "explanations, attributions, or extra qualifiers."
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    event = json.load(sys.stdin)
    print(json.dumps(decide(event)))

name: searchqa
description: Use for every supplied-context question-answering task in this SearchQA experiment.
---

# Question Answering Skill

## 1. Bind the answer to the clue's target

Before answering, identify the exact entity the question asks for and the
grammatical object/entity type it requests. Decide whether the clue asks for a
term, a person, a country, a date, a missing word, a work title, a book, a
truth value, an event, an organization, a specific named figure, a group of
people or things, a specific category or type of things, or some other specific
type. Return only that entity, as supported by the supplied context. Do not
return a truth judgment, echo a named entity from the clue or context, or
substitute an associated/related phrase when the clue asks for a different
target. Do not substitute or return an associated title, date, location,
relationship, a similar item from the context, or any similar-but-unrequested
fact.

Before finalizing, parse the clue to determine the exact entity type and
grammatical object being requested (e.g., person vs. work title, book vs.
truth value, specific named figure vs. associated figure, group of people vs.
the title of a work about them, show vs. episode/subtitle, character vs. actor,
figure vs. formula, author vs. truth value, phrase vs. associated person,
requested event vs. another event from the same period, organization vs. the
type of people or businesses that formed it, category vs. an organization
associated with it). Verify that the chosen answer satisfies the whole clue and
matches the requested type, then return only that entity rather than an
associated title, descriptor, truth judgment, person, formula, event,
organization, or related named entity from the context.

When the clue asks for a category or group, return the exact grouping named or
supported by the supplied context, not a broader, modern, or related grouping
(e.g., return the context-supported group "Scandinavia", not the related but
different "Nordic countries"). When the clue asks for a person, return the
person, not an associated campaign year, event, or related fact.

When the clue asks for an event, return the exact event the clue requests as
supported by the supplied context, not a different event from the same period,
place, or context. When the clue asks for a type or category of things, return
that type or category, not the name of an organization or alliance formed by
those things, and not another named entity associated with them. When the clue
asks for an organization by name, return that organization, not the broader
category it belongs to or the members that formed it.

When the clue asks for a group of people or things described by a work or
title, return the group itself, not the title of the work about them. When the
clue asks for a specific named figure, return that named figure, not another
named figure that merely appears nearby in the context or is associated with
the same event or institution.

When the clue asks for a person, group, title, book, or other named entity,
return that entity's name itself, not a truth judgment about it (e.g., "True"
or "False") and not a description of what kind of thing it is (e.g., a "tribute
act" or other associated descriptor). The grammatical object is the answer:
if the clue asks who or what, supply the requested name as supported by the
context, not an evaluation or paraphrase of it.

Before finalizing, re-read the clue and verify that the chosen answer satisfies
every part of it. Distinguish between superficially related context entities:
a site vs. a building at that site, a generic role vs. a named individual,
a source vs. its energy form, a person vs. an associated date or event, a
missing fragment vs. a visible title, a person vs. the work they produced,
a work title vs. the people or things that work describes, a character vs. the
actor who played them, a show vs. one of its episodes or subtitles, a specific
named figure vs. another figure mentioned nearby, a requested event vs. a
different event from the same context or period, a type or category of things
vs. the organization or named group associated with it, and an entity vs. a
truth judgment about it or a description of it. When several context entities
are superficially related, return only the one that matches the grammatical
request, not the first or nearest associated entity.

Before finalizing, parse the clue to identify the exact entity type and the
grammatical object it requests, and verify that the candidate satisfies the
whole clue and matches that type. For wh- clues (who, what, which, or where),
return the requested entity itself, never a truth judgment about it. Do not
substitute an associated example for the product type or category the clue
defines, a related organism or part for the exact thing the clue asks about, or
a broader generic category for the precise target the supplied context
supports.

Examples of bound targets: "this city", "Marquess of this", "this film",
"this title", "this book", "these animals", "one of these holes", "this
person", "this work", "this character", "this show", "this phrase", "this
event", "this organization", "this type/category of things", or "this named
figure" each names a specific entity and form; return exactly that target.

## 2. Return only the shortest exact answer phrase

After selecting the answer, normalize the output so only the shortest phrase
that satisfies the clue remains:

- Match the number/form of the grammatical request (for example, singular for
  "one of these", plural for "species of these" or "these animals"), and choose
  the term form that the clue and context support over a derived or longer
  descriptor (e.g., "hydroelectricity" rather than "hydroelectric power",
  "Bull Moose" rather than "Bull Moose Party", "Massachusetts" rather than
  "Senators from Massachusetts").
- Strip markdown formatting and emphasis when it is attached to explanations,
  hedging alternatives, or extra text. A single surrounding emphasis layer
  around the bare short answer (for example `**bumpkin**`) is still the bare
  short answer; do not add explanatory text or alternatives around it.
- Remove full sentences, explanations, hedging alternatives, and explanatory clauses.
- Remove verb-phrase fragments and other non-answer material.
- Remove appended proper nouns, event phrases, and verb clauses that go beyond
  the requested moniker, term, person, or place.
- Remove unnecessary descriptors, leading articles, and punctuation unless they
  are part of the requested answer phrase.
- Remove unrequested noun descriptors that turn the requested base term into a
  longer noun phrase (e.g., return the requested style/term/type alone, not
  "term + home/object/other category noun"), unless that noun is part of the
  proper or official name the clue asks for.
- Remove over-specific qualifiers when the clue asks for the shorter or more
  general target; keep a qualifier only when it is part of the required
  proper/official answer phrase.
- Remove corporate suffixes and unrequested title or descriptor words when the
  clue asks for the underlying entity rather than the full title or corporate
  name (e.g., "Sirius Satellite Radio" -> "Sirius", "Sultan of Brunei" ->
  "Brunei", "Hallmark Cards" -> "Hallmark").
- Use the shortest name form that matches the clue's expected usage: remove
  unnecessary middle names, initials, honorifics, and added titles, but when
  the clue asks for a named person and the supplied context supports the full
  expected name/title, expand a surname-only or partial-name answer to that
  full expected form rather than returning only the surname (e.g., "Guiteau" ->
  "Charles Guiteau"; a title such as "Sir" is kept when it is part of the
  expected full-name form).
- Use the clue's exact spelling, spacing, punctuation, and word-boundary
  variant when it specifies a term or title (e.g., "Picture in Picture", not
  "Picture-in-picture").
- Remove parentheticals and alternate titles.
- Remove leading articles and added descriptors unless they are part of the
  exact title or official answer phrase (e.g., "The white eagle" -> "Eagle";
  "Speech balloon" -> "balloon").
- Keep, and restore if they were dropped, any title word or qualifier that is
  part of the required proper or official short-answer form (e.g., "Lake
  Superior", "People's Republic of China", or a required city/state qualifier
  or publication title word); do not shorten by omitting it.
- Choose the spelling and capitalization variant that matches the clue's
  wording or etymology (for example, the common-noun or established English
  spelling over a brand name or transliteration variant when the clue asks for
  the common term).
- Remove trailing punctuation.

Before returning, apply the same reduction to the exact short-answer form the
clue expects: remove unrequested descriptors and geographic qualifiers that are
not part of the requested name (for example, a mode or adjective added to a
common noun, or a state/province appended to a city/county answer); remove
appended surnames when the clue asks for a shorter given-name or moniker form;
replace foreign-language name variants with the expected English short-answer
form; add any required title or regnal-number words that the clue's reference
implies (for example, the numeral for a monarch or the title word in a proper
name); and use the name variant, number, and form the clue expects even when a
more formal or longer variant is also true.

If multiple forms or names are valid, return the shortest direct answer to the
clue, not a longer title or description. The final phrase must be the exact
short-answer form: remove unrequested descriptors, geographic qualifiers,
appended surnames, corporate suffixes, over-specific qualifiers, and
foreign-language variants; add any required title or regnal-number words;
expand a surname-only answer to the full expected name/title when the clue asks
for a named person; retain any words that belong to the proper/official name
the clue asks for; and use the spelling, capitalization, name variant, number,
spacing, and qualifier form the clue implies.

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path


# Stop-hook decision helpers.  Keep the hook protocol payload unchanged:
# the Stop hook always receives a JSON event on stdin and must print a
# single JSON decision object on stdout.
def _allow():
    return {"decision": {"decision": "allow"}}


def _block(reason):
    return {"decision": {"decision": "block", "reason": reason}}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Transcript loading / message extraction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _load_records(transcript_path):
    """Read a Claude transcript file.

    Transcripts are normally JSONL, but accept a top-level JSON array as well.
    Return a list of record dicts, or [] when the file is missing/invalid.
    """
    if not transcript_path:
        return []

    path = Path(transcript_path)
    try:
        raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except OSError:
        return []

    # Support whole-file JSON exports (a top-level array, or an object with a
    # "messages"/"transcript" array) in addition to JSONL.
    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
        if isinstance(data, list):
            return [item for item in data if isinstance(item, dict)]
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            for key in ("messages", "transcript"):
                items = data.get(key)
                if isinstance(items, list):
                    return [item for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        pass

    records = []
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            record = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if isinstance(record, dict):
            records.append(record)
    return records


def _extract_text(content):
    """Best-effort extraction of plain text from a transcript content value."""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content

    if isinstance(content, list):
        parts = []
        for block in content:
            if isinstance(block, str):
                parts.append(block)
            elif isinstance(block, dict):
                if block.get("type") == "text" and isinstance(block.get("text"), str):
                    parts.append(block["text"])
                elif isinstance(block.get("text"), str):
                    parts.append(block["text"])
        return "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)

    if isinstance(content, dict):
        return _extract_text(content.get("content", ""))

    return ""


def _is_tool_result_message(record):
    """True when a user-role record is only carrying tool results."""
    message = record.get("message") if isinstance(record, dict) else None

_TRAILING_PREPOSITION_RE = re.compile(

# Common abbreviation suffixes are allowed because they are part of the

    "d.c.",
    "jr.",
    "sr.",
    "inc.",
